Ryan Braunberger

Democratic-NPL candidate for Secretary of State, North Dakota · Challenger

North Dakota state senator (District 10) and Democratic-NPL Senate Minority Caucus Leader; independent contractor

Ryan Braunberger is a Democratic-NPL state senator from Fargo who has represented District 10 in the North Dakota Senate since December 2022 and serves as Senate Minority Caucus Leader. He is the Democratic-NPL nominee for Secretary of State and faces incumbent Republican Michael Howe on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot.

Where Braunberger stands

Election security
Says North Dakota's elections are secure, free and fair. Notes that every ballot is paper, including the printout from express voting machines, and that the paper is what gets counted. Says state IT staff constantly monitor for hacking threats.
Voter data sharing with the federal government
Says North Dakota should keep protecting its citizens' privacy. Argues it would be hard for a secretary of state to share the voter data because the Department of Transportation owns it.
Mail-in voting
Says President Trump's executive order on mail-in voting, which the Supreme Court struck down, would have disenfranchised North Dakota voters. Notes that 35 of the state's 53 counties have only one polling place and rely heavily on mail voting.
Local control of elections
Says he would focus on fair elections and on letting local governments control their own elections. Cites efforts by Gov. Armstrong and Secretary Howe to stop Fargo's approval voting system.
Voter confidence and turnout
Says the state needs to boost confidence in election systems and increase civic engagement. Argues that unproven claims about election integrity create mistrust.
